reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that single-pass artifact processing introduces correlated blind spots—such as glob filter limitations or pagination truncation—that can silently propagate errors. To counter this, dual counting enforces orthogonality by using two independent enumeration strategies (e.g., Git refs vs. branch listings), ensuring any discrepancy signals a failure mode. Seeded spot-checking adds a probabilistic layer, validating a fixed subset of artifacts for full-text integrity, SHA-256 parity, and canonical IDs. This prevents silent drift where partial ingestion or schema hollowing goes undetected. The word-boundary guard prevents accidental mutations during remediation by enforcing regex boundaries around numeric literals, avoiding contamination of immutable identifiers like Twitter snowflakes. These safeguards collectively ensure that each wave's data integrity is maintained through mathematical consistency checks and controlled transformation rules.
